_comment: Which books exist and how they are built from the pools in tools/library/. See tools/build_books.mjs. One book per (number of shapes, board size); each runs through every difficulty tier, easiest first. A puzzle is in at most one book.
_sparseShare: Within each shape and tier a book only draws from the sparsest share of the puzzles (fewest blocked cells), as far as that leaves enough: the original L-panel puzzles have few black squares, and a book that takes puzzles by difficulty alone is mostly dense.
_tierWeights: Share of a book each tier gets (1 unless listed). Read as counts for a 1000-puzzle book: 100 Beginner, 450 Medium, 450 Hard (Beginner is the least interesting tier, so it is small). A tier with too few puzzles gives up what it cannot fill.
_shapeWeights: Relative share of a book each shape (or pair) gets within a tier; unlisted shapes weigh 1. The 'boring' shapes weigh a third: they can only make Beginner or Medium puzzles that all use the same single technique (the line pieces domino, I tetromino and I pentomino, and the rigid pentominoes T, U, V, Z and X). A rebuild only adds puzzles unless run with --trim, so new weights take full effect with --trim.

groups.name: One shape
groups.blurb: Every tile is the same shape. Each book runs from Beginner to Hard.

groups.name: Two shapes
groups.blurb: Each tile is either of two shapes. Each book runs from Beginner to Hard.

groups.name: Sparse
groups.blurb: Every tile is the same shape, with very few black cells, like the original L-panel puzzles. Mostly Medium and Hard.

tour._comment: The first puzzles of this book are a shape-by-shape introduction: `perShape` easy puzzles of each shape in turn, before the rest of the book in difficulty order.
